sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Stone Platform** is the final location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Stone Platform inside the Erdtree is a flat, circular surface encircled by dense fog and sparsely covered with saplings, tree roots, and metallic gold leaves. Suspended above the platform is the stone husk of Queen Marika, crucified upon a massive Rune Arc and impaled through the abdomen by a red needle. The fractured, crumbling goddess was imprisoned here after shattering the Elden Ring.

The Stone Platform is accessed from the Elden Throne at Leyndell, Ashen Capital, though the path is initially blocked by Godfrey, First Elden Lord. The Tarnished is transported to this realm after passing through the Erdtree's impenetrable thorns and touching its golden light. A cutscene plays and the final battle against Radagon of the Golden Order begins.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Sun** is a celestial body in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The sun rises in the northeast and sets in the southwest, matching the movement of the stars. The sun remains fixed in the eastern sky at Crumbling Farum Azula and never sets at Enir-Ilim. It is seen at its brightest from the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, but cannot be seen from Caelid, Altus Plateau, Mt. Gelmir, or the Mountaintops of the Giants.

The sun once held profound significance in the Lands Between. In an age long past, it illuminated a great city with its brilliance. It was served by Azula Beastmen and Skeleton Knights, both of whom are now among Those Who Live in Death. However, the Seat of the Sun has since faded into obscurity.

The gentle warmth of the sun was later emulated by the Erdtree, which once healed the lands that basked in its golden glow. Although sunlight was felt more vividly in the Realm of Shadow, its rays could not penetrate the darkness of the Abyssal Woods.

sections.heading: Eclipse
sections.markdown:
Like the Moon, the sun manifested in different ways. One such form was an eclipsed sun drained of its color. This frigid sun of Sol served as the symbol of the Wandering Mausoleums, offering a star's protection to the soulless Demigods. It was a bulwark against Destined Death and held the power to imbue life into soulless bones.

The knights of Castle Sol were mesmerized by the frigid eclipsed sun. They fervently prayed for it to appear, hoping the dreadful event would call a spirit into the soulless demigod interred with their mausoleum. They planned to return the life of Godwyn the Golden on behalf of Miquella the Kind. However, it never came to pass. While the exact cause of their failure is unclear, this sealed the fate of the Haligtree.

 - Beast Skeleton Knights carry the Sun Realm Shield.
 - Ruin Fragments and Sanctuary Stones interact with light. Sanctuary Stones blessed with Two Fingers incantations become Warming Stones.
 - Farum Azula was destroyed by a meteor impact in time immemorial.
 - The sun remains fixed in place in the eastern sky when viewed from this location.
 - Enir-Ilim
 - It would nestle perfectly atop the Gate of Divinity.
 - A prominent sundial appears at the center of the ashen arena where Miquella's Followers are fought. The orientation of this clock holds importance as it is exactly as it appears in concept art for the area.
 - The sun never sets in this location.
 - Potent Sunwarmth Stones are made from Spiritgrave Stones harvested from the adjacent Gravesite Plain.
 - Several circular motifs above doorways may symbolize the sun.
 - Stormveil Castle
 - Like the Gate of Divinity, there is an intentional trough built into the two primary towers.
- The warm sun variant may be—or may have once been—connected to the Fell God.
 - The Furnace Visage, depicting the fell god, resembles a sun. It appears on the Furnace Golems, where it sits high above the heads of Fire Giants depicted on their knees.
 - The sun medallion worn by the Dung Eater symbolized his guiding grace and his Mending Rune of the Fell Curse. Reddish hair strands grow from the excised horns on his Omen Armor.
 - Queen Marika's victory over the fell god coincided with the growth of the Erdtree, which once radiated the warmth of the sun.
- An eclipse likely occured in the past, possibly giving rise to the soulless king Ensha.
- The failure of the eclipse plan may have been a consequence of the Starscourge Conflict, when Starscourge Radahn halted the movement of the stars. It is also possible the revival was prevented by the Prince of Death setting the colorless eclipsed sun ablaze with his flames, spreading Death in the process.

sections.markdown: Spirits** (霊, *Rei*), **souls** (魂, *Tamashii*), **phantoms** (幻影, *Gen-ei*), **sprites**(精霊, *Seirei*), **vengeful spirits/rancor** (怨霊, Onryō), and **wraiths** (呪霊, *Jurei*) are states of being in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Spirits are the remnants of the dead. Not everyone can see or hear spirits. Spirits are generally defined by their ability to appear out of thin air, be summoned by Spiritcaller Snail, or be immune to Status Effects. Some spirits are fully ethereal, while others are wholly physical. Other types of spirits exist somewhere in between.

Spiritcaller Snails, Wandering Mausoleums, Commander Niall, Commander O'Neil, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, Tibia Mariners, Large Sanguine Albinaurics, and the Tarnished can all summon spirits.

The **Soul** is inherently tied to the Elden Ring, and dwells within living beings. They are alive, and can be killed without killing the body, and vice versa. It can be projected out of the body in the form of a Phantom, allowing it to be summoned by others. Sorcerers imbue their souls into Primal Glintstone, allowing it to be transferred into new bodies. Upon death, souls return to the Elden Ring, currently via the Erdtree, presumably to be born into new bodies.

Souls came into being when the One Great was fractured by the Greater Will long ago.

Souls were imbued into weapons by the stone Golem Smiths of the ruined forges.

The spirits of the dead are left to wander without some form of guidance. The Tibia Mariners were the first gravekeepers and have always lent their leadership. Like the Grace of the Erdtree, a lamplight is said to guide the spirits of fallen warriors the spirit to the Helphen. Spirits destined for Erdtree Burial followed the blue light of Rosus guides the spirits of the dead to the catacombs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The terms used for Soul in the Japanese script generally refer to the animating consciousness which dwells within living beings and reincarnates upon death, while the term used for Spirit generally refers to the spectral presence left behind by the dead, more akin to a ghost. This distinction seems to hold in Elden Ring, with souls being reborn through the Erdtree and spirits lingering in the form of ashes and such.
- An individual's body, soul, and spirit are connected but separate parts of one's identity.
 - The Deathbirds used ghostflame to separate spirits from ashes.
 - The Furnace Golems use a form of Messmerfire to burn bodies down to the soul.

- Various types of unusual souls and spirits appear in the game.
 - Fia's Champions are manifestations of the warmth and vigor siphoned from the many heroes held by Fia, Deathbed Companion.
 - The Dung Eater binds his victims' spirits to his own body.
 - Like Ulcerated Tree Spirits, the Ancestral Spirits and their horned remains are fully corporeal. They gain new abilities and shine brighter after absorbing the spirits of animals.
 - Though Serosh is normally ethereal like a spirit, he can turn corporeal at will.
 - Puppets are usually corporeal, but sometimes appear as phantoms.
 - The short-lived Larval Tears that sprout from spiritgraves are neither flesh nor spirit; they are a unique form of life somewhere in between.
 - D, Hunter of the Dead and D, Beholder of Death are one soul with two minds and bodies.
 - Like Marika and Radagon, Miquella and St. Trina were two entities sharing the same body. When Miquella shed St. Trina, she gained an independent, physical body.
 - Divine Elements like Scarlet Rot and Messmerfire are able to inhabit and grant life to Putrid Corpses. Those Who Live in Death may function similarly.
- Non-living things can be imbued with spirits or souls.
 - Primeval Sorcerers transfered their souls to primal glintstones.
 - Warrior Jars can harness the combined power of the champions they contain. When heroic Alexander, Warrior Jar finally cracks, Jar Bairn is selected to inherit Alexander's Innards and fighting spirit.
 - Golem Smiths read wrinkles in metal to grant souls to Molten Tears and Smithscript weapons.
 - The spirits of white banners appear over the sites of the major battles of the Shattering, including in the Altus Plateau, Capital Outskirts, and Wailing Dunes. The spirits of fiery red banners are present in the boss arena for Gladius, Beast of Night.
 - Many ancient gravestones on the Gravesite Plain turned into spiritgraves, the eldest of which have already faded away. Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon transforms her Juvenile Scholars into spiritgraves when she rebirths them with the amber egg.
 - Ashes of War are the essence of mighty techniques.

- Sprites are drawn to holes, where they form nests. Conversely, spirits naturally are drawn to Grave Violets and Gloveworts Spirit Tuners use these to bolster spirits. Grave Keepers used Spirit Glaives to commune with spirits.

- Spirits can be permanently destroyed by the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
The Tarnished** is the protagonist of Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

Compelled by the "Flame of Ambition", the Tarnished endeavors to brandish the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. In their journey throughout the Lands Between, they encounter various demigods, bearers of Great Runes, as well as their fellow Tarnished.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: A Tarnished of no renown, called to cross the sea of fog to the Lands Between, having been blessed once more by the Grace once thought lost to their kind. Their origins are unknown, as are their accomplishments prior to their arrival in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
The Tarnished begins their journey in the Chapel of Anticipation, off the western coast of Limgrave, where they find only the corpse of a Finger Maiden slumped against a wall, implicitly the one originally intended to be theirs. After a brief encounter with a Grafted Scion, the Tarnished falls from the precipice and washes up in the Stranded Graveyard. Although death seems inevitable, they are found by a mysterious woman riding a spectral steed. The woman grants the Tarnished two flasks: one of crimson tears and the other of cerulean tears. With these blessings, the Tarnished emerges from the damp cavern into the grasslands of Limgrave.

The Tarnished is reunited with the woman once more, and she introduces herself to them as Melina. Seeing that the Tarnished is maidenless, she offers to play the role of a Finger Maiden, allowing the Tarnished to convert the Runes they collect from their enemies into strength. In return, she requests that the Tarnished bring her with them to the foot of the Erdtree. To aid them further, Melina grants the Tarnished a whistle which will allow them to call upon her spectral steed, whose name she reveals to be Torrent. Melina further explains to the Tarnished that she is searching for a purpose given to her by her mother inside the Erdtree long ago, and the reason she lives, despite her burnt and spectral state. She advises the Tarnished to seek the Great Runes: shards of the shattered Elden Ring, currently held by the Demigods.

Early in their shared journey, Melina extends the Tarnished an invitation to Roundtable Hold, the gathering place of Tarnished champions. Here, the Tarnished meets several of their fellow Tarnished, as well as Roundtable Hold's leader, Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing.

The Tarnished claims a Great Rune from one of the Shardbearers scattered throughout the Lands Between, and is permitted audience with the Two Fingers; envoys of the Greater Will, and Finger Reader Enia. Interpreting the words of the Fingers, Enia explains to the Tarnished that the shattering of the Elden Ring has left the land in ruins, and instructs the Tarnished to hunt down the Demigods, who have been renounced by the Greater Will. Gideon offers the Tarnished further advice, imparting his knowledge of the five Shardbearers known to Roundtable Hold.

On their journey, the Tarnished may encounter Ranni the Witch, a Demigod and the perpetrator of the Night of Black Knives. The Tarnished may choose to enter her service, aiding her as she treads the dark path of the Empyrean and attempts to establish her Order upon the world.

After claiming two Great Runes, the Tarnished makes their way to Leyndell, Royal Capital, the home of Morgott the Grace-Given. Melina regains the ability to govern her own movement and bids the Tarnished farewell, leaving them with Torrent and the ability to convert Runes into strength. The Tarnished proceeds to the Elden Throne and defeats Morgott, claiming his Great Rune, but when they attempt to pass through the door in the Erdtree's trunk they find the way obscured by impenetrable thorns. Melina appears before the Tarnished once more, and reveals that it is her purpose to help the Tarnished become Elden Lord. In order to do so, however, the Erdtree must be burned to remove the thorns. And so, the Tarnished begins a new journey with Melina, to the Mountaintops of the Giants, upon which rests the giant's forge, and a flame which may burn the Erdtree.

The Tarnished may encounter a being named Shabriri, who reveals to the Tarnished that Melina must offer herself as kindling so that the Erdtree can burn. Shabriri offers an alternative: the tarnished may take Melina's place as kindling and singe their own flesh instead. To this end, they must descend below the Royal Capital and meet with the Three Fingers, setting themselves upon the path to becoming the Lord of Chaos. Should the Tarnished accept this offer, they will make an enemy of Melina, who vows to hunt them down and kill them if they rise as Lord of Chaos.

Whether through Melina's sacrifice or the power of the Frenzied Flame, the Erdtree is set aflame, and the Tarnished is transported to Crumbling Farum Azula; an ancient temple in the sky said to have been crumbling since time immemorial. In Farum Azula, the Tarnished encounters and kills Maliketh, the Black Blade, releasing the Rune of Death upon the Lands Between.

The Tarnished returns to Leyndell to find it coated in ash, the Erdtree glowing red above. The Tarnished makes their way through the ruined city, but their path is blocked by Gideon, who attempts to stop them from becoming Elden Lord. The Tarnished kills Gideon, who asserts with his dying breath his belief that a Tarnished cannot become a Lord, for a man cannot kill a god.

The Tarnished once again finds themselves at the Elden Throne. This time they find Godfrey, the First Elden Lord and former leader of the Tarnished. Godfrey reveals that he has come to once more be granted audience with Queen Marika, the goddess of the Lands Between The two Tarnished duel, and Godfrey is forced to tear the beast Serosh from his back and assume the role of Hoarah Loux. Nevertheless, the Tarnished defeats Godfrey and approaches the Erdtree.

Inside the Erdtree, the Tarnished find Marika hanging from a Rune, her body seemingly made of stone. Marika falls from the Rune and her body begins to warp as she assumes the form of Radagon of the Golden Order, the second Elden Lord. Radagon fights to protect the Golden Order from the Tarnished, but is bested. From his body emerges the Elden Beast, a vassal of the Greater Will and embodiment of Order that became the Elden Ring long ago. Despite its status as a god, the Tarnished fells the Elden Beast, and finally stands before the broken body of Queen Marika. Depending on the decisions they made on their journey, the Tarnished may now decide the fate of the Lands Between. They may repair the Elden Ring and rise as Elden Lord, go with Ranni on her thousand year voyage into the chill night, or become the Lord of Frenzied Flame and incinerate all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.markdown: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, the Warrior is generally considered a bad option. For pure Dexterity builds, Samurai generally outclasses the Warrior due to the higher Intelligence, Mind and Arcane stats of the Warrior generating too many wasted points, while Astrologer and Prisoner are able to outclass it in Intelligence/Dexterity hybrid builds. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Demi-Human Queen's Staff
sections.markdown:
Despite the unfortunate position of the Warrior, it does have a specific niche where it is considered the optimal choice, which is a pure Dexterity build that also uses between 10 and 12 Intelligence in order to cast low-level spells. Prisoner will become optimal if the intelligence required is any higher than 12, but within this range of intelligence, the Warrior origin can use the Demi-Human Queen's Staff which provides a relatively high spell scaling value for low intelligence casters, allowing for spells that deal a reasonable amount of damage. The spells that can be used within this range are:

- Glintstone Pebble
- Glintstone Stars
- Scholar's Armament

sections.heading: Overview

A great ethereal tree forms in Limveld when the Night threatens the Lands Between. Emitting a ghostly white glow, its spiraling trunk branches into two enormous hands, their wooden fingers extending into a broad canopy. Although quite small on the first day, it grows as the Expedition progresses. It reaches its full size by the end of the second night, enveloping a Divine Tower without a discernible entrance.

The interior of the divine tower closely resembles the other divine towers of the Lands Between but is entirely bleached white with roots coming down from its ceiling. There is a pool of blue water, a Site of Grace, a Smithing Table, and a petrified Merchant. A doorway leads to a bridge outside, where the sky is purple and chaotic. The bridge is structurally similar to those found at divine towers; however, its pedestals lack statues. At the opposite end of the bridge, a large gate is embedded within the trunk of a petrified tree.

After the defeat of the boss of the second night, a large, jelly or sap-like mass appears within the Ring of Reign. Interacting with the substance transports the Nightfarers inside the tower. They walk onto the bridge to reach the great door. Opening it together, they release a dark fog and gain audience with the Nightlord.

These web-weaving creatures snip with sharp pincers and deliver venomous stings with their tails. Some possess insectile wings, a mutation granted by the primordial Crucible. They come in three sizes, are vulnerable to Fire damage, and are commonly found in hornsent-associated areas.

Small scorpions were prepared into a traditional meal in hornsent culture. After the Church of the Bud was burned by Messmer the Impaler during his crusade against the Land of the Tower, the scarlet rot was discovered in its ashes. Soon after, giant Spider Scorpions began to spread throughout the Realm of Shadow.

These ambush predators often dangle from the ceiling or perch high on walls, waiting to drop down on unsuspecting prey.

sections.markdown: The **Spiraltree**, also known as the **spiral tree**, is the sigil of a faction in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion for Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: The spiral tree was a hornsent symbol that was later adopted by members of Messmer's Army in the Realm of Shadow. Although granted abundant grace by Queen Marika, the invaders who carried out her crusade were unable to gaze upon their beloved Erdtree. While the belief that Marika would one day end the crusade persisted amongst her greatest zealots, many crusaders accepted Marika's betrayal or simply lost their faith over time. They were subsequently captivated by the majesty of Enir-Ilim stretching upward to reach the gods, and soon a secret new faith spread amongst the forlorned Erdtree people. They depicted the spiral tree in white on sullied amber jewels and used their faith to cast incantations that replicated the sorceries and divine invocations of the hornsent.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: The Spiraltree consists of two entwined trunks spiraling around a central stake in a double helix. Each trunk ends in a spray of branchlets that frame a pair of hands reaching skyward from atop the pillar.

sections.heading: Notes

- The spiraltree displays whenever the player or Inquisitors cast Spiral Incantations.
- The spiraltree is nearly identical in appearance to the Spirit Shelter in Elden Ring Nightreign. Both include twinned trunks wrapped around a tower and a large pair of upward reaching hands.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: This page lists **Statues** in Elden Ring, Shadow of the Erdtree, and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The people of the Lands Between have always erected statues to celebrate the deeds of their heroes and deities. Some of these ancient characters only appear as statues, including the bearded god of the Ancient Dynasty and the goddess queen of the Rauh civilization.

During the Age of the Erdtree, statues of Queen Marika appeared in churches and other places used by her followers. When Radagon of the Golden Order became Marika's second Elden Lord, statues in his likeness establishing "Golden Order Totality" were used in churches, as well. A sculptor contracted for Radagon's statue at Leyndell, Royal Capital discovered his true identity and hid the secret in the statue.

Maleigh Marais, Shaded Castle Castellan commissioned hundreds of statues supposedly depicting Malenia, Blade of Miquella following her brief visit to the Shaded Castle after the Battle of Aeonia.

sections.heading: Queen Marika Statues
sections.markdown: Statues of Queen Marika the Eternal include Stakes of Marika and Effigies of Marika. Statues of Marika with two braids of equal length portray her before she offered her Golden Braid to the Grandmother at the Shaman Village.

sections.heading: Lord Radagon Statues
sections.markdown: Statues of Radagon of the Golden Order render him in his signature Golden Order Totality pose.

sections.heading: Lord Godfrey Statues
sections.markdown: Statues of Godfrey, First Elden Lord were placed in front of pre-existing Serosh statues at Stormveil Castle, representing their shared identity. The statues are separate models.

sections.heading: Demigod Statues
sections.markdown: Statues portray scenes from Miquella and Malenia's youth.

sections.heading: Ancient Dynasty Statues
sections.markdown:
The Ancient Dynasty erected countless statues of a nameless, one-eyed bearded god. The bearded old patriarch of the Ancient Dynasty appears in several forms.
- He is shown on the Stone Coffins and The Four Belfries.
- In the Siofra River and Ainsel River, he holds half a tablet, standing on its discarded twin. Roots or branches enwreath his legs, similar to Radagon’s imagery.
- At the Cocoon of the Empyrean, he appears without legs, still clutching his tablet.

Bald, bearded elders also appear on the Winged Scythe.

sections.heading: Champion Statues
sections.markdown: Statues of a hooded male figure depict him either wielding an Iron Greatsword or holding an open book. In Leyndell, Royal Capital, Misbegotten pray directly to this statue.

sections.heading: Grand Lift Statues
sections.markdown: Grand Lifts include statues of Tree Sentinels, Scholars, and Fire Monks.

sections.heading: Hero's Grave Statues

sections.heading: Rauh Statues
sections.markdown: Large statues of a nameless goddess-queen wearing an octagonal crown appear throughout the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, an area strongly associated with the Crucible. Kindred of Rot in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh worship a statue of the Crucible goddess. The Verdigris Discus is located beneath another of her statues. These links associate both her and the Crucible with the outer god of rot.

sections.heading: Rosus Statues

- Skeletal Knights are the undead remains of honored Sun Realm soldiers. They wear crimson capes that display a sun.
 - They are encountered in graveyards across the Lands Between, often in proximity to castles and forts once associated with Banished Knights, Ancient Dragons, or Dragon Communion.
 - Skeletal Knights with gold bones spawn near moangraves in the Capital Outskirts.
 - Beast Skeleton Knights carrying the Sun Realm Shield defend Crumbling Farum Azula, but do not wear red capes.

- The identity of the "**Sun Realm**" or the city once called the "**Seat of the Sun**" remains unclear. It may refer to one—or none—of the following locations:
 - Crumbling Farum Azula
 - Some Skeleton Beastmen wield shields of the Sun Realm.
 - Ruin Fragments and Sanctuary Stones interact with light. Sanctuary Stones blessed with Two Fingers incantations become Warming Stones.
 - Farum Azula was destroyed by a meteor impact in time immemorial.
 - The sun remains fixed in place in the eastern sky when viewed from this location.
 - Leyndell, Royal Capital (past)
 - Some Sun Realm soldiers rise from the massive graveyard in the Capital Outskirts. The Moangraves of this graveyard indicating a civilization with unique burial customs.
 - The Revenger buried at Castle Morne was the only survivor of a country now vanished, and was buried under a Moangrave just like those outside Leyndell
 - The arsenal charm wielded by the Revenger and derived from his greatsword is found in the Altus Tunnel, implying his presence in the area before moving to the fringes and Castle Morne.
 - As the soldiers of the civilization that used Moangraves were massacred by the times of Godfrey and its last survivor fell trying to get revenge on the Elden Lord, Leyndell would have developed over the ruins of a previous city, now lost to time.
 - Sun Realm soldiers found in graveyards of Limgrave and Caelid would be explained by Marika banishing to the fringes those that did not accept her Order after conquering Altus.
 - Stormveil Castle
 - Some Sun Realm soldiers are found at graveyards close to Stormveil Castle, Summonwater Village and Mistwood Ruins
 - Like the Gate of Divinity, there is an intentional trough built into the two primary towers.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Torrent** is a spectral steed and the player's mount in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Torrent is a spectral steed resembling a horse and a goat with two short horns on his head and a white mane. Prior to meeting the Tarnished, he is in the company of Melina. The pair find the Tarnished unconscious in the Stranded Graveyard, where Melina reassures Torrent before granting the Tarnished two flasks. Later, when the Tarnished enters into an accord with Melina, she grants them the Spectral Steed Whistle which allows them to call upon Torrent, revealing that Torrent has chosen them.

Torrent has a taste for Rowa Raisins, Sweet Raisins and, in particular, Frozen Raisins, which can be used to restore his health. His former master entrusted Ranni the Witch to deliver the Spirit Calling Bell to his next master.

Should the Tarnished choose to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame and incinerate the Erdtree, a final cutscene will show Melina picking up the Spectral Steed Whistle, which disintegrates in her hand (though the player still has access to it in-game).

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: The player can acquire Torrent from Melina at any time by either resting at the **Gatefront Ruins** or **Agheel Lake North** sites of grace or after touching three different sites of grace then resting at any of the additional graces:

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.markdown:
Besides allowing a player to get around relatively quickly, Torrent also doesn't appear to take fall damage from certain heights. This allows one to easily jump down from heights that'd normally kill the player as long as they're mounted on Torrent. That said, Torrent isn't immune to dying from jumping from too high of a height: even if a double jump is used to get to a lower level, if the starting point is too high up, Torrent will dissipate on landing and the player will die from the impact.

Jumping again while in mid-air will cause Torrent to perform a second jump. This can only be done once until he touches the ground again and can be used to change direction at the moment of the second jump.

Players can also fight from horseback against enemies, such as shooting arrows or casting spells. However, only one of the player's weapons can be used at a time as the left hand is constantly occupied holding Torrent's reigns, it is still possible to switch between the right-hand and left-hand armament while riding by using the same input the player uses to two-hand their weapons.

Note that it is not possible to change from wielding a weapon one-handed to two-handed while mounted. It is however possible to get the bonuses of two-handing by performing the action before mounting up.

Spirit springs can be used by jumping while riding Torrent to reach higher altitudes. Landing on or close to a spirit spring will completely negate fall damage.

Torrent's HP can be restored by consuming Rowa Raisins, Sweet Raisins and Frozen Raisins. Using a Flask of Crimson Tears will also restore his health on top of the player's own, however only while the player is riding him. If Torrent is killed, using the Spectral Steed Whistle will bring up a prompt to expend a single charge of the Flask of Crimson Tears to revive him.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Torrent cannot be summoned in Dungeons, Legacy Dungeons, and the Abyssal Woods, or during online multiplayer sessions.

It has the unique disadvantage of starting out at 77.97% equip load, exceeding the 70.00% threshold of Heavy Load, resulting in slower, shorter rolls. The easiest way to correct this is to remove either the Halberd they are carrying (for a Longsword-focused build) or the Helmet they are wearing (if wishing to carry both weapons) or the Longsword and the Gauntlets (for a Halberd-focused build). Alternatively, increasing Endurance to 15 will also get them down to Medium Load, letting them roll normally.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.markdown: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, Vagabond is the most effective choice for several build types. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Strength + Dexterity
sections.markdown:
The primary benefit of Vagabond is that it saves a total of 5 levels when compared to Wretch across its Intelligence, Faith and Arcane stats. Builds that require at least 14 Strength and at least 13 Dexterity while also not investing in the other three stats will find Vagabond to be the most optimal origin. For builds that also wish to minimize the Mind stat, the Hero origin is able to tie with Vagabond in efficiency, but the Hero is not able to outclass Vagabond outright for a build that only increases Strength and Dexterity out of the five damage-increasing stats.

If a build requires fewer points in Strength than 13, Samurai becomes the most efficient option. If a build requires fewer points in Dexterity than 13, Hero becomes the most efficient option.

sections.heading: Strength + Intelligence
sections.markdown:
For a build that focuses exclusively on Strength and Intelligence as its damage-increasing stats, Astrologer and Hero are tied for being the most optimal starting origin to choose. However, Vagabond will share a tie with Astrologer if the build also requires at least 13 Dexterity, with 4 fewer stat points wasted compared to Wretch. This makes Vagabond an optimal choice for Strength + Intelligence builds that use weapons with high Dexterity requirements such as:

- Royal Greatsword
- Loretta's War Sickle
- Onyx Lord's Greatsword
- Troll Knight's Sword

sections.heading: Strength + Faith
sections.markdown:
Similarly to Strength + Intelligence, Prophet and Hero are tied by default for the most efficient starting class for a build exclusively utilizing Strength and Faith investment to increase damage. However, Vagabond is the most efficient option for a build that also requires at least 13 Dexterity, wasting 4 fewer stat points compared to Wretch. This makes Vagabond the optimal choice for Strength + Faith builds that use weapons with high Dexterity requirements such as:

- Golden Halberd
- Siluria's Tree
- Ordovis's Greatsword
- Magma Wyrm's Scalesword
- Blasphemous Blade
- Grafted Dragon
- Devourer's Scepter
- Gargoyle's Black Blades

sections.heading: Dexterity + Faith
sections.markdown:
By default, Prophet is the most efficient starting origin for a build that exclusively invests in Dexterity and Faith to increase damage output. However, if the build also requires 14 or more Strength, Vagabond becomes more efficient, wasting 4 fewer points compared to Wretch. This makes Vagabond the optimal choice for Dexterity + Faith builds that use weapons with high Strength requirements such as:

- Sacred Relic Sword
- Treespear
- Godslayer's Greatsword
- Golden Order Greatsword
- Vyke's War Spear

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Possessed of great strength and abundant Grace, Queen Marika's mounted Tree Sentinels met little resistance as they charged down her enemies. Heavily-equipped and blessed with old Erdtree incantations, very few were permitted to join their nigh unbreakable ranks. They were resolute in their commitment toward protecting that which deserved protection, becoming the gold standard to which all defenders of the Erdtree measured themselves. Their gallantry influenced the practices of the Leyndell Knights, who similarly put the shield before the sword.

After the Ancient Dragon Gransax attacked Leyndell, some of the Tree Sentinels adopted characteristics of the Ancient Dragons. These knights became Draconic Tree Sentinels to better protect the Erdtree.

A few Tree Sentinels embarked on Messmer's crusade, later safeguarding the path to the Shaman Village, Queen Marika's former home.

King Morgott distributed special, invisibility-revealing torches to the Tree Sentinels following his rise to power, hoping to prevent a second Night of Black Knives.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: An imposingly sturdy knight chained to the saddle of a large horse. The Tree Sentinel wears golden filigreed plate with intricate vine and floral motifs, inlaid with crimson and viridian jewels, and a dark ochre cape depicting a sacred tree. Their helm features red false eyeslits and a small, decorative tree with yellow-green growth in place of a plume. The knight carries a massive golden halberd imbued with Holy energy. Their steed is covered head-to-hoof in barding of golden plate over layered black armor. Its ornate chamfron (faceplate) has vented blinkers and a spiral unicorn horn embellishment.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Those Who Live in Death** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Those Who Live in Death are humanoid skeletal creatures of variable height and equipment, characterized by their ability to resurrect upon initially being slain. This can be prevented by killing them with certain sources of holy damage, or by attacking their bones before they resurrect. They are commonly found in catacombs, graveyards, and around Deathroot. Those Who Live in Death are a product of the spread of Deathroot following the Night of Black Knives and the death of Godwyn the Golden, and fall outside the principles of the Golden Order. It is for this reason that Golden Order fundamentalists known as hunters are tasked with exterminating them, down to the last.

Those Who Live in Death are extremely weak to holy damage. They can be summoned by and occasionally found alongside Tibia Mariners.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
On the Night of Black Knives, a stolen fragment of the Rune of Death enabled the Black Knife Assassins to murder Godwyn the Golden, which marked the first death of a demigod in history. However, Ranni the Witch, a co-conspirator of the assassins, perished at the same moment by carving the cursemark of Destined Death, also known as the mark of the centipede, into her flesh. This resulted in the cursemark, which should have taken the shape of a circle, splitting into two half-wheel wounds, in turn allowing Ranni's body to perish, while Godwyn died in soul alone. Ranni lingered on as a spirit, while Godwyn was unable to die a true death, and instead continued to live within death, without a soul, becoming known as the Prince of Death.

As the first dead of the demigods, Godwyn was buried under the capital, at the Erdtree's roots. After the night of the dire plot, the Rune of Death spread across the Lands Between through the underground great tree roots, sprouting in the form of Deathroot, a source that causes those who come into contact with it to become Those Who Live in Death. Those Who Live in Death have refused the call to return to the Erdtree, and trespass beyond life's bounds. It is for this reason that they exist outside the principles of the Golden Order, and hunters among the Golden Order fundamentalists arose to exterminate defiled reason—all for the perfection of the Order. In turn, Maliketh, the Black Blade, from whom the fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen, took on the guise of Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman, and consumed Deathroot gathered for him by hunters in order to sate his appetite.

Despite the distaste for Those Who Live in Death, some of the Tarnished sympathized with them upon their return to the Lands Between, including Fia, Deathbed Companion, Lionel the Lionhearted, and Sorcerer Rogier. According to Rogier, Those Who Live in Death have committed no offense, have every right to life, and have simply touched upon a flaw in the Order.

During the time of The Tarnished (Protagonist), D, Hunter of the Dead discovered the mark of the centipede in Summonwater Village, in Limgrave, and brought it back to the Roundtable Hold. He was later murdered by Fia, who wished to return the cursemark, also known as the hallowbrand, to Godwyn. When tracked down to the Deeproot Depths, Fia reveals that she was the companion of Godwyn, the Prince of Death, and wished to be a mother and guardian to Those Who Live in Death.

Upon giving her the Cursemark of Death obtained from Ranni's corpse, Fia claims it will allow Godwyn to claim a second illustrious life and take his rightful place as the First of the Dead. She will lay with Godwyn in order to conceive a child that will serve as the new life of Godwyn, that will take the form of the rune of Those Who Live in Death. Fia asks The Tarnished (Protagonist) to brandish her child and become their Elden Lord by staying the persecution of Those Who Live in Death. Embedding the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince into the Elden Ring, it will restore Death and embed the principle of life within Death into the Order.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Turtles** are wildlife enemies in Elden Ring. They are non-hostile and will withdraw into their shells when antagonized.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Turtles held deep symbolic significance to those who dwelled in the Lands Between. They were considered wise beasts that possessed boundless stamina and power. Two-headed turtles were prized by the hornsent who saw their intertwining necks as a reflection of the sacred spiral.

In the southern regions, turtle neck meat was considered a highly nutritious delicacy. Their flesh was often prepared in medicinal solutions by nomadic peoples or pungently pickled by the forager brood. However, these practices were by some considered an act of barbarism, given the reverence of turtles.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Turtles in the Realm of Shadow are wizened and covered in long strands of hair. A modest outcrop of horns grows on the wrinkled heads. In contrast, the common turtles of the Lands Between are reddish and experienced no sprouting.

When attacked, turtles retreat into their protective shells. The natural roundness of their shell acts as a shield to deflect most enemy attacks.

The Tibia Mariners were the first of all grave keepers in the Lands Between, beckoning Those Lost in Death by blowing into their hollow oars. They guided the dead to the Gravesite Plain for an eternity, unbothered by their bones having long since crumbled to dust. Their secrets were inherited by future generations of grave keepers, such as the Servants of Death, who used their skulls as catalysts for summoning wandering spirits. Their boats, or recreations of them, were prominently displayed at the Shadow Keep. The importance of the oarsmen was recognized even amongst the living.

The Tibia Mariners were suppressed when the Rune of Death was removed from the Elden Ring. In their absence, those without Marika's Grace who met a glorious end in battle were left to wander. The heroes of her Golden Order received Erdtree Burial, and had no need for the archaic ferrymen. When Godwyn the Golden was buried at the base of the Erdtree, he soon transformed into the piscine Prince of Death. The blight leaked from his body and infected the great tree roots, and manifested itself as Deathroot throughout the Lands Between. The Tibia Mariners slowly resurfaced, and Those Who Live in Death answered their call.

Gurranq the Beast Clergyman charges D, Hunter of the Dead, and the Tarnished to hunt down the Tibia Mariners and reap their Deathroot. He believes he can restore the sanctity of the Golden Order by absorbing the residual fragments of Destined Death.

sections.heading: Mountaintops of the Giants
sections.markdown: A Tibia Mariner encountered on a cliff face overlooking Castle Sol upon the Mountaintops of the Giants. Unlike other Tibia Mariners, this one does not have a health bar. sections.heading: Charo's Hidden Grave
sections.markdown: A Tibia Mariner at Charo's Hidden Grave solemnly patrols a quiet river flanked by fields of iridescent crimson lilies. When frightened, he teleports up a small waterfall and summons a Royal Revenant. If pushed further, he eventually retreats behind a large aggregation of gravestones where several strong skeletons await his call.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown:
- While the Tibia Mariners themselves, curiously enough, are not counted as among Those Who Live in Death, their minions are, and the usage of specialized anti-undead equipment will make it easier to isolate the mariner.
- In terms of combat ability, these enemies are pretty weak on their own, especially against ranged attacks. Their main threat comes from the allies they summon and the fact that they typically operate in large combat areas, periodically teleporting to different positions.
 - Given that they all fight among ruins, it can be challenging to locate them after they teleport, and the constant stream of summoned allies can become overwhelming. To counter this, your primary tactic should be to ignore the summoned allies entirely. Instead, use Torrent whenever possible to quickly locate the mariner, then hit them hard and fast before his friends have a chance to regroup.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
The seated Tibia Mariner uses an to paddle his incorporeal rowboat across ethereal, violet waters. His body is skeletonized, save for the wizened beard that clings to his slack mandible. A floral pattern decorates the white-laced chapel veil that rests upon his head and drapes over his bony frame. Attached to the veil are wide, golden hoops, each adorned with three large golden flower emblems inlaid with rubies. The mariner's forearms are wrapped in cloth, and several gold bracelets hang from his wrists. He wears the tattered remains of robes sewn from purple thread.

The mariner's transparent wooden rowboat shimmers with a faint purple hue. A chair is built into its deck, with a semi-circle cut into the backrest to create a depression at the top. Spiral patterns ascend its stile and backpost before transitioning into straight lines beaming upward. The backpost extends several feet higher than the chair and terminates in an upward concave arch reminiscent of Marika's Rune. Hanging ventrally from it is a small lantern alight with a purple ghostflame. The boat's exterior hull is highly decorated with intricate relief carvings. Two adjacent floral embellishments are encircled by spiral-containing rings and bound together with a sturdy knot. The gunwale trim above features a wavelength weaving over and under stars, possibly symbolic of the Primeval Current.

The mariner will sometimes whip up a grand torrent of water that carries his boat high into the air. When it reaches it apex, he extends his arm, and a bright red light emanates from a jewel in his palm. This light is said to beckon the lost spirits of those slain in battle.

The dry and metallic moans of the mariner eerily echo upon themselves as if uttered from deep within a dungeon. When he sounds his lengthy brass horn, a single clang of metal deeply reverberates like a tolling bell. When cast, his ancient Death magic produces a haunting noise, akin to the crashing of cymbals.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Soundtrack: *Death's Kindred*
- The enemies summoned by Mariners vary by location. Some call Giant Skeletons or Royal Revenants, while others only field assorted Skeletons.
- Their movement was not restricted to water when they appeared in the Lands Between.
- They appear to be leaders among Those Who Live in Death, and each one carries Deathroot.
- Only one non-boss Tibia Mariner can be encountered. They are in the Mountaintops of the Giants, north-west of the Snow Valley Ruins Overlook Site of Grace.
- The Tibia Mariners lack of Holy damage vulnerability may be attributed to being part spirit.
- In Elden Ring Nightreign, the Tibia Mariner will appear at the end of a day, leading a large group of Those Who Live in Death.
- Mariners are grave keepers who ferry lost souls across a sea in the spirit world.
- The detailing on the external hull of the mariners' boats may be interpreted as an infinity symbol (∞) representative of an endless cycle of life and death.
- Tibia's boats appear at the Shadow Keep. Each is a funeral pyre carrying a Messmer's Army standard, representative of Tibia ferrying the unsung heroes of Messmer's crusade.
- The ancient mariners themselves were laid to rest amongst the crimson fields of Charo's Hidden Grave.
- Tibia Mariner remain seated as if immovable like an Elder Albinauric or the giant maidens perched upon Eternal City chair-crypt.
 - The also known as the shinbone or shankbone, is the larger, stronger, and anterior (frontal) of the two bones in the leg below the knee. The first generation of Albinaurics lost the use of their tibias, and are unable to walk on their own.
 - Some of the red Second-Generation Albinaurics at the Mohgwyn Palace blow into wooden clubs like horns to summon the mariners' Giant Skeleton.
 - The massive figures seated in the Chair-Crypts of the Eternal Cities vaguely resemble the Tibia Mariners. However, upon closer inspection, their outfits and chairs are quite different.
 - The Putrescent Knight also suffers this affliction.
- It is unclear whether the Tibia Mariners played a role in delivering the Stone coffins now beached on the Cerulean Coast.
- Usher of Death, Rosus fills a similar role, guiding the dead toward the catacombs and Erdtree Burial.
- Crescent Moons are carved into the side of the boat.
